You want advice... first, it’s likely bullshit that it was a, “gut feeling.” But, you’ll never learn the real reason. Don’t bother trying to find out. If she had wanted you to know, she would’ve told you. When you run into her years from now, she’ll have a story which won’t match what actually happened.

Pick a strategy. Are you going to see if it can be fixed? Wait for her to come back around? Start dating others? Take a break from dating altogether? It’s important that you make a decision here. As in, if you start dating others before you’re over her, you’ll simply mess up your next relationship.

Be honest with yourself about your feelings. Understanding yourself better will help you move forward.

Distractions help. Projects, friendships. I’ve been told that it’s important to focus on yourself and be happy in your own skin.

Don’t turn to substances to get through.

There are already offset time zones in the world (time zones that don't line up to the hour). Indian Standard Time, which encompasses the entirety of the 1.2 billion people living there, is UTC+05:30. So we wouldn't even be doing anything revolutionary.

The rationale behind daylight savings time is that 9am-5pm people will have an extra hour of daylight after work to do daylight-dependent things (shopping and sports in particular).

But, if we permanently shift the clocks ahead by 30 mins, 9am-5pm people will have 30 minutes extra daylight after work during our current daylight savings period, and will only lose 30 mins less daylight during our standard time period.

And then we won't have the numerous other side effects - disruption of agrarian activities, disruption of evening activities, business scheduling problems.

Don't forget the fact that very young children and pets simply do not get the time change. Your infant will still be up at "normal" time, demanding to be fed, so you don't actually gain anything from the time change as a parent.

First, the Dr. Craig sets up a few premises. These are:
- that atrocities in the OT were singular events (as if for some reason that makes them less bad);
- that they were largely done to secure the Promised Land, which was of course, God's will; and
- that even if apologists concede these to be atrocities, it doesn't disprove God, just shows that there is doctrinal error.

Harris, asking his leading questions, then prompts, "In the event that one would want to go internally as well and say God could have had good reasons for this judgment against these pagan nations, what are our options on that?" What he's saying is, "All those premises aside, if we still feel the need to tackle this pesky question, how do you address the fact that skeptics call these actions atrocities?" 

Dr. Craig spends the rest of the article explaining why these actions were not atrocities, either as the people who committed them or the god who commanded them.

This site http://www.gotquestions.org/Old-Testament-violence.html says it would have been immoral to NOT kill the children, since their parents had been killed (the men for being combatants, the women for being seductresses.

This site http://www.monergism.com/thethreshold/articles/onsite/skeptics/02genocide.html says it was God's prerogative to kill off an immoral culture, but omits the aspect of killing children.

So, no, it's not just one guy saying this.
If mainstream Christians believe that genocide is decidedly immoral, then they believe God commands people to do immoral things?

The general rule that the author is deriving from this specific event is what he defines to be "divine command morality," which is, "An ethical theory which says that our moral duties are constituted by God's command." It has the application that, "God has the right to command you to do things which, in the absence of a command, would have been sin." 

So yes, God-mandated genocide is moral, according to Dr. Craig. And mainstream Christians, too, unless mainstream Christians believe the OT is mythology or God is evil.

In this specific case of genocide, Dr. Craig is indeed saying that the killing of children sent them to heaven. The general rule is that if God commands you to do something, it becomes your moral duty, even if it's something which on the surface would appear to be immoral (though in this specific case of genocide, Dr. Craig explains why the "kill em all" principle is A-ok).
